complexity.name: Some work
complexity.note: A few things to get right

steps.do: Heat the pan with a splash of oil.
steps.cue: The oil thins out and slides easily

steps.do: Add the courgettes in one layer. Leave them alone.
steps.why: Stirring straight away drops the heat and they stew instead of browning.
steps.cue: Edges going golden

steps.do: Beat the eggs into the cream with salt and pepper.
steps.why: Season this properly — it's the only chance.

steps.do: Layer the courgettes in a dish. Pour the egg mix over. Lay the cheese on top.
Bake until golden.
steps.why: Give the dish a nudge. If the middle still wobbles, it needs longer.
steps.cue: Top browned, centre firm

steps.do: Put a big pan of water on. Salt it well.
steps.why: It should taste like a light broth. This is the only chance to season the pasta itself.

steps.do: Warm the oil with the garlic in a second pan.
steps.cue: Garlic smells sweet, not brown

steps.do: Add the tomatoes. Let them collapse.
steps.cue: Darkened and thick, not watery

steps.do: Cook the pasta. Keep a mug of the water before you drain.
Tip the pasta into the sauce with a splash of that water. Toss hard.
steps.why: The starch in the water is what makes sauce cling. Without it, it slides off.
steps.cue: Sauce coats every piece

steps.do: Cook the potato and onion in plenty of oil.
steps.why: Keep it gentle. Any browning here makes the tortilla bitter.
steps.cue: Soft enough to squash, still pale

steps.do: Beat the eggs. Drain the potatoes and stir them in. Leave it to sit.
steps.why: The rest lets the potato soak up egg. That's what holds it together.

steps.do: Pour into the pan. Cook until the edge sets.
steps.cue: Edges firm, middle still loose

steps.do: Flip it using a plate. Slide it back in.
steps.cue: Centre stays slightly soft

steps.do: Cook the rice. Spread it on a tray to cool.
steps.why: Warm rice steams instead of frying. Cold, dry grains are the whole trick.

steps.do: Get the pan properly hot, then add the oil.
steps.cue: A drop of water skitters and vanishes

steps.do: Fry the onion, then the courgette.
steps.why: Don't crowd the pan. Too much at once cools it and you end up stewing.
steps.cue: Catching colour at the edges

steps.do: Add the rice. Press and turn it.
steps.cue: A dry rattle, not a wet hiss

steps.do: Push everything aside. Scramble the egg in the gap. Fold it through with soy.
Boil the potatoes. Start these first.
steps.cue: A knife slides in with no resistance

steps.do: Pat the fish dry, then oil and salt it.
steps.why: Wet fish steams and turns grey. Thirty seconds with kitchen paper changes the result.

steps.do: Roast the fish.
steps.why: Press it rather than trusting the timer — cod goes from perfect to chalky in about two minutes.
steps.cue: The flesh just parts when pressed

steps.do: Crush the potatoes with oil. Squeeze the lemon over everything.
steps.why: Lemon at the end. Added early it cooks off to nothing.

steps.do: Get the pan hot and dry, then add a little oil.
steps.cue: The oil shimmers and moves like water

steps.do: Brown the pork on every side. Do it in batches.
steps.why: Crowding the pan means no colour, and the colour is where the flavour comes from.
steps.cue: Deep brown crust on each face

steps.do: Add garlic, fish sauce and a splash of water. Put a lid on.
steps.cue: Barely a bubble

steps.do: Take the lid off and turn the heat up. Let it reduce.
steps.cue: Sauce is glossy and drags behind the spoon

steps.do: Serve over rice with lime and pepper.
Cook the onion slowly in oil.
steps.why: Rushing this is the main reason a home curry tastes thin.
steps.cue: Soft, floppy, going gold

steps.do: Add the spices straight into the oil. Stir for half a minute.
steps.why: Ground spices need fat and heat. Thrown into liquid they stay dusty.
steps.cue: You can smell them across the room

steps.do: Add the tomatoes. Cook them down.
steps.cue: Oil separates and pools at the edges

steps.do: Add the chickpeas and coconut milk. Simmer.
Stir the spinach in at the very end.
steps.why: About forty seconds. Longer and it goes grey.

steps.do: Take the steaks out of the fridge and salt them. Boil the potatoes meanwhile.
steps.why: A fridge-cold steak burns outside and stays cold inside.

steps.do: Heat a heavy pan dry until it's genuinely hot.
steps.cue: A drop of water skitters across and disappears

steps.do: Lay the steaks in. Don't move them.
steps.why: Moving the meat stops the crust forming. One side at a time, no fiddling.
steps.cue: Dark crust when you lift a corner

steps.do: Add butter, garlic and thyme. Spoon the foaming butter over the meat.
steps.cue: Butter foaming, not browning black

steps.do: Rest the meat as long as it cooked. Crush the potatoes into the pan juices.
steps.why: Cutting early tips the juice onto the board instead of keeping it in the meat.

steps.do: Soften the onion and pepper in oil.
steps.cue: Limp and glossy

steps.do: Stir the cumin and paprika into the oil for half a minute.
steps.why: Same rule as any spiced dish — bloom them in fat first.

steps.do: Add the tomatoes and let them thicken.
steps.why: Too loose and the eggs sink instead of sitting in wells.
steps.cue: A dragged spoon leaves a trench

steps.do: Make wells, crack the eggs in, put a lid on.
steps.cue: Whites set, yolks still soft

steps.do: Serve straight from the pan with bread.

recipes.name: Oat porridge with banana and honey

steps.do: Bring the oats and milk up slowly, stirring.
steps.why: Slow and stirred releases the starch. That's what makes it creamy rather than lumpy.
steps.cue: Thick enough to hold a spoon

steps.do: Add a pinch of salt near the end.
steps.why: It won't taste salty. Without it, porridge tastes of nothing.

steps.do: Top with banana, honey and cinnamon.
Blend the chickpeas with tahini, lemon and garlic. Add cold water until it moves.
steps.why: Cold water, not more oil — it lightens instead of weighing it down.

steps.do: Keep blending well past the point it looks finished.
steps.why: Smoothness is time, not equipment.
steps.cue: No grain left on the tongue

steps.do: Spread it out, pool oil in the middle, dust with sumac.

recipes.name: Yoghurt bowl with honey and oats

steps.do: Toast the oats in a dry pan.
steps.cue: They smell nutty and turn a shade darker

steps.do: Spoon them over the yoghurt with banana, honey and cinnamon.
steps.why: Layer rather than stir, so the textures stay separate.
